difficulty.rationale: Standard AP C FRQ-style item. Requires choosing conservation of angular momentum about the pivot (the pivot force exerts no torque about it) and justifying non-conservation of mechanical energy in the inelastic collision. Part B is a symbolic derivation with the bullet's point-mass angular momentum m v L plus the combined rotational inertia, followed by a simple numeric evaluation. answers.brief_reasoning: Disagree. The bullet embeds in the rod, so the collision is perfectly inelastic and some kinetic energy turns into thermal energy and deformation. Mechanical energy is not conserved. The pivot force acts at the pivot, so it exerts no torque about the pivot. Gravity is vertical and its torque is negligible during the short impact. So angular momentum about the pivot is conserved. Linear momentum is not conserved, because the pivot exerts a horizontal impulse.
answers.final_answer: Disagree. Kinetic energy is lost in the inelastic collision; angular momentum about the pivot is conserved.

answers.brief_reasoning: Angular momentum about the pivot is conserved: mvL = (ML²/3 + mL²)ω. Solving gives ω = mv/[(M/3 + m)L] = 20/(1.1×0.8).
